system.summary: Four systems. De Burgo's (also used by de Laude): one sign per letter, 2-3 homophones for common letters, many vowels dropped, word signs (ro = et, g t 4 a ŧ o = quod, 93 = Cesar/Maiestas Vestra, ⊞ = pro). Fürst: glyph-letter substitution for single words inside clear Latin, plus sign-names. Gattinara: digit/symbol letters, homophones, name signs (struck x c + o = Maiestas, S°p° = principis Caroli). Colla and Modena: own alphabets, not analysed.

solution.what: Web search for an edition or decipherment of de Burgo's / Fürst's 1510-12 cipher reports.
Found the full-size AIS image route and walked the archive plan to resolve all 27 shelfmarks to AIS IDs; downloaded ~240 images.
Surveyed every page of all 27 items for cipher and gloss coverage.
Rebuilt Veit von Fürst's alphabet from glossed words in 22-3-8 (15 signs).
Rebuilt de Laude's (= de Burgo's) alphabet from his glossed lines, three passes (~45 signs); control 31/37 letters.
Deciphered the unglossed 26-4-9 'Delta' paragraph; LM used only to rank skeleton matches.
Rebuilt Gattinara's alphabet from glossed words, three passes (31 signs); S°p° = principis Caroli; 23-5-4 l. 17 read 2/3 groups.
Deciphered Gattinara's 23-5-47 postscript ll. 4-5; 'maiore [?]' ranked from m?iore.
Systematic de Burgo sign table from ~60 glossed words in 22-3-18 and 25-2-27: 43 letter-sign rows, 6 word signs; control 15/17 letters (not blind).
Fifth pass on the 26-4-9 Δ. paragraph with the full table: 34/195 tokens firm (17%), 50 with uncertain words.
Regesta Imperii XIV and Tomokiyo searched on the web for these reports.
Completed Fürst's June-July 1510 alphabet and read the 59 unglossed groups: 40 firm, 13 in part, 6 open; control 4/4 held-out glossed groups exact.

outcome.method_basis: Contemporary interlinear decipherments cover nearly all ~2,100 cipher lines; the project identified them (AIS records none for 24 of 27 items) and is rebuilding the keys from them to read the unglossed residue.
